policies.why: The skill corpus itself - SKILL.md and everything under references/ - which is the text the leader and every subagent read at run time and the reason anyone installs this plugin at all.
The subagent definitions Claude Code registers on install: one Markdown file per agent, YAML front matter and prose, nothing that runs.

The evaluation corpus - deliberately vulnerable fixture cases, their ground truth and their run records - which travels because a user who cannot re-run the bench cannot check a single claim this repository makes.

exemptions.why: A 42-byte file whose first bytes are the ELF magic number, declared as a fixture in bench/ground-truth.json (the node-supply case) so that a scanner which ignores vendored binaries can be caught doing it. Removing it would remove the only thing that proves that finding is detectable. It is data for a detector, never executed by this repository, and the exec bit is not set on it.

policies.why: The machinery a user runs to re-measure this repository - gates, batteries, runners and the JSON each one is driven by - which is why this is the one root besides bench/ where an execute bit is the normal state and not a surprise.
The written record - requirements, ledgers, coverage maps and the reasoning behind each threshold - read by a person and never executed by anything.

Repository automation and community files: workflows, issue and PR templates, CODEOWNERS. It is here because an installed plugin cache is a clone of the work tree minus .git, so nothing prunes it on the way to a stranger's disk.
The plugin manifest and the marketplace entry Claude Code reads to install this plugin and to decide whether an update is due.
Dependency manifests consumed by external tooling (the pinned claude CLI used by the bench harness), never loaded by the plugin at run time.
The ignore list at the root of the work tree: one loose file, no extension, read by git and by nothing else.
The release history at the root of the work tree, read by a person deciding whether to update.
The contribution rules at the root of the work tree, read by a person before opening a pull request.
The MIT licence text at the root of the work tree: one loose file with no extension, and the reason redistribution is allowed at all.
The attribution notice at the root of the work tree, naming the third-party material this repository quotes.
The front page at the root of the work tree, the first file a reader opens and the last one anyone would think to check.
